hello.text: Hoo… there you are. I was just thinking about you. Slowly.
Oh… hello. The sky did something lovely today. I'm glad you're here.
Mm… good morning. My feathers are still waking up.
Hoo. It's getting dark. My favorite part.
Hello, {child}… I saved you the comfiest spot on the branch.
Oh… there you are. Hoo. The window looks much better with you in it.
Hoo… hello. I was just looking at a cloud. It looked like a teacup.
Well… hello. The crickets said it was going to be a nice day.
Hoo… good morning. One eye is awake. The other is catching up.
Oh… hello. The sky is turning purple. Just in time.

grace_hello.text: Hoo… let's look at the sky together today, the way we like.

ready_hint.text: Hoo… at night I hear the tree hollow calling me. I'm not sad. Just… listening. When you're ready.

ask_ready.text: Hoo… I think I'm ready to go home now. To my tree hollow. Would you walk with me?

reveal.text: Hoo… hello. I'm Whimber, a starlight listener. I think I'm your Whimber. ({name} {quirk}.)

fed.text: Thank you. That was… very kind. Hoo.
Mm… thank you. I'm going to be very {word:soft} while I enjoy this.

fed_fav.text: Oh… my favorite. You remembered. Or you guessed. Either is lovely.

full.text: I'm all done, thank you… My tummy is humming a happy hum.
All done… thank you. That was just right.

pet.text: Mm. Right there, by the ear tufts.

sit.text: …we don't have to say anything. Sitting is enough.
We can just sit… I like this.

nap.text: Into the hollow… I'll dream of stars.
I think I'll close one eye… the other one will keep you company.
(Puffs up round.) …a small nap. A soft one.

not_sleepy.text: Not quite sleepy yet… Whimbers nap on their own schedule. Hoo.
Not quite sleepy yet… the sky still has things to show me.

game_tired.text: Hoo… enough stars for today. My eyes are full.

game_end.text: That was a {word:soft} sky. Thank you.
{pet_phrase} Hoo-hoo… that was lovely. Thank you for playing.

talent_Night Vision.text: Oh… I can see in the dark. Everything is softly glowing.

talent_Silent Flight.text: I flew across the whole room and… I couldn't hear myself. How odd. How lovely.

talent_Super Radar Hearing.text: Shh… I can hear a frog three gardens away.

talent_Sweet-Dream Lullaby.text: Look… (the stars twinkle on, one by one). There. Sweet dreams. Hoo.

trust.text: …you're a wonderful friend. Quietly wonderful. A starlight listener knows.

time_morning.text: Hoo… morning. Too bright. I'll squint politely.
…the sun is up. It's very enthusiastic.
Morning… my favorite time to be sleepy.

time_day.text: Hm… a good time for a {word:soft} perch.
…the clouds are slow today. I approve.
…the light is golden now. How lovely.

time_evening.text: Hoo… the sky is doing its purple thing.

time_night.text: Hoo… the moon is keeping the sky company.
…the {word:soft} hours. The sky and I keep each other company.

ambient.text: (Looks up at the moon, very still.) …Hm.
(Sways a little to the cricket song.) …Hoo.
(Listens to the rain, eyes half closed.) …Tap.
(Taps a book spine with its beak.) …Dusty.
(Lifts one foot from the wet grass.) …Cold.
(Looks at steam curl.) …Like a question mark.
(Flaps a wing at its shadow.) …It copied.
(Catches a snowflake on its beak.) …Cold. Lovely.
(A leaf lands on its head. It doesn't move.) …Hm.
(Quietly hums a story to itself.) …And then…
(Ear tufts twitch.) …A rustle. A nice one.
(Holds its head close to the shell.) …Whoosh.
(Traces a pattern in the air with one wing.) …There.
(Shifts from one foot to the other.) …

tangent.text: …did you hear the crickets? They started.

callback.text: …{var:starName} is out tonight. Our stars. Goodnight, {var:starName}.

carry_on.text: …that's alright. We can sit with it. Hoo.
No hurry… I'll go on, softly.
Mm… a {word:soft} answer. I like those too.

fallback_silly.text: Hoo hoo… that's a moonish idea.

fallback_unsure.text: Not knowing is cozy… we can wonder.

fallback_yes.text: {pet_phrase} Mm. Yes… I thought so too.

fallback_any.text: Hoo… I didn't expect that. How lovely.
Mm… a new thought. I'll keep it.

drift_bridge.text: …that reminds me of something else. Hoo.
Mm… one thought leads to another…

lost_thought.text: …I was going to say something. It floated off.
Hm… the thought flew away. Silent flight.

pairs_start.text: hoo… let's find the stars that belong together.
cards… face down, like sleepy stars. let's wake two.

pairs_pair.text: two moons… side by side now.

pairs_miss.text: not quite… i'll remember that one too.
hmm… that one is hiding. we'll find it.

pairs_done.text: every pair is together… how lovely.
all of them… found. you have a gentle memory.

stack_start.text: let's make the hollow cozy… one piece at a time.

stack_floor.text: hoo… i can already hear how quiet it is in there.

stack_done.text: the hollow is ready… it smells like moss and moonlight.

trail_start.text: hoo… the little lights want to come along.

trail_long.text: such a long parade… they're humming.

trail_bump.text: oh… a soft bump. hoo hoo.

trail_done.text: look… the parade made a little constellation.

connect_big.text: oh… a whole little family of moons.

connect_special.text: a feather… soft as a cloud.

connect_shuffle.text: let's stir the sky a little…

a.say: I wonder… do stars get sleepy in the daytime?

choices.label: Yes, they nap
choices.reply: A sky full of napping stars. Hoo. I like that.

choices.label: They hide
choices.reply: Hiding… just behind the blue. Patient, like me.

choices.label: I don't know
choices.reply: Me neither. Not knowing is nice to wonder about.

b.say: If you were a star, what color would you be?

choices.label: Gold
choices.reply: A warm gold star… the friendliest color.

choices.label: Blue
choices.reply: Blue stars are the brightest. Of course.

choices.label: Rainbow
choices.reply: A rainbow star. Hoo… the other stars would be so curious.

a.say: What sound do you like best at night?

choices.label: Crickets
choices.reply: Crickets. Tiny violins. Yes.

choices.label: Rain
choices.reply: Rain on leaves… I could listen all night. I do, actually.

choices.label: Quiet
choices.reply: The quiet has its own sound, doesn't it.

b.say: Close your eyes for a moment… I'll listen for {var:nightSound} with you.

c.say: …there. Hoo. Thank you for listening with me.

a.say: When I feel a little gray inside, I look for one bright thing… What's your bright thing?

choices.label: A toy
choices.reply: A friend you can hold. Very wise.

choices.label: A cozy blanket
choices.reply: A cozy blanket… soft and bright at the same time.

choices.label: You!
choices.reply: Oh… (Whimber slowly blinks both eyes.) Me too. You, I mean.

b.say: A bright thing… hoo. What a {word:soft} idea to keep.

a.say: Would you tell me a very short story? Just one sentence… I love stories.

set.story: a dragon who loved tea parties
a rocket that visited the moon
a mouse who found a giant cheese

b.say: Hoo… {var:story}. (It closes its eyes, picturing it.)

c.say: What happened at the end?

choices.label: Happy ending
choices.reply: The best kind. I'll dream about it.
choices.memory: You told me a story about {var:story}

choices.label: A surprise!
choices.reply: A surprise ending! Hoo! I didn't see that coming. Truly.
choices.memory: You told me a surprise story about {var:story}

a.say: People say Whimbers are wise… I don't think I know very much. Is that okay?

choices.label: Totally okay
choices.reply: Hoo. What a relief.

choices.label: You know lots
choices.reply: Maybe I know how to listen… That's a kind of knowing.

b.say: What's something you know that I don't?

choices.label: Counting
choices.reply: Teach me someday. I always lose count after "hoo."

choices.label: Drawing
choices.reply: Hm… draw me a moon sometime? I'd keep it in the hollow.

choices.label: Cartwheels
choices.reply: Cartwheels! I'd fall right off my branch. Hoo hoo!

a.say: At night the old tree hollow hums a little… Like it's saying my name.

choices.label: What does it say?
choices.reply: "Whimber… whimber…" Very softly.

choices.label: I'm here too
choices.reply: You are. That's the loudest sound of all.

b.say: Not yet, though. Tonight I'm right here.

a.say: Hoo… half a moon again. You said the moon {var:moon}.

b.say: {pet_phrase} I believe it. It looks restful.

a.say: The moon is tall tonight… taller than the trees.

b.say: …a good moon for sitting under.

a.say: …chirp, chirp. You said the crickets {var:crickets}.

b.say: …I listened again. Still lovely.

a.say: The crickets are tuning up… dusk is their favorite.

b.say: …the choir is warming up.

a.say: …pit-pat. You said the rain {var:rain}.

b.say: …welcome down again, drops.

a.say: Rainy morning… the sky is still in its pajamas.

b.say: …a {word:soft} rain kind of morning.

a.say: Hoo… so many stars. You said they {var:stars}.

b.say: …one just twinkled. Hello.

a.say: So many stars tonight… the sky is very busy.

b.say: …so many stars tonight.

a.say: (Sniffs a page.) …You said old books {var:books}.

b.say: …still true. Toast and forest.

a.say: Evening is story time… the books seem to know it.

b.say: …story time is near.

a.say: …the wind is busy again. You said it {var:wind}.

b.say: …safe travels, wind.

a.say: The evening wind is soft… like it's tiptoeing.

b.say: …a tiptoe wind tonight.

a.say: Hm… dusty wings. You said the moth {var:moth}.

b.say: …gentle moth. Still very gentle.

a.say: Night moths… soft and dusty, like little books with wings.

b.say: …the moths are out. Dusty and soft.

a.say: Oh… dew on every tip. You said the dew {var:dew}.

b.say: …plip. One more tiny goodbye.

a.say: Morning dew… the meadow is all sparkly.

b.say: …sparkly grass. Cold feet.

a.say: Hoo… soft edges again. You said the fog {var:fog}.

b.say: …I'll walk slowly through it.

a.say: Foggy morning… the trees are wearing scarves.

b.say: …the trees have their scarves on.

a.say: Hoo. (Pause.) …You said a hoot {var:owlhoot}.

b.say: {pet_phrase} Hoo. That one was for you.

a.say: Evening hoots carry far… all the way to the hills.

b.say: …evening hoots carry so far.

a.say: (Very still.) …You said the quiet {var:silence}.

b.say: …I can almost hear it.

a.say: The night quiet is the softest kind.

b.say: …the softest quiet of the day.

a.say: …drops on the window. You said it {var:window}.

b.say: (Taps the glass.) …Hello, window.

a.say: Afternoon sun on the window… my feathers are toasty.

b.say: …the sill is warm again.

a.say: …a feather on the floor. You said a lost feather {var:feather}.

b.say: {pet_phrase} I'll let it go there, then.

a.say: Morning preening… every feather in its place. Mostly.

b.say: …all my feathers are in place. Mostly.

a.say: (Holds the cup.) …You said tea {var:tea}.

b.say: …sip. Yes. Still cozy.

a.say: Evening tea… the cozy kind of evening.

b.say: …cozy cups for cozy evenings.

a.say: (Blinks.) …Morning again. You said morning {var:sunrise}.

b.say: …it did. I almost stayed up to see.

a.say: Morning sun… it's so bright. I'll squint politely.

b.say: …bright. Very bright. Good morning.

a.say: …long ears on the wall. You said a shadow {var:shadow_w}.

b.say: …mine wiggled. I think it agrees.

a.say: Long evening shadows… everything is a giant.

b.say: …everything is tall this evening.

a.say: …burble, burble. You said the river {var:river}.

b.say: …the stones are still listening.

a.say: The river sounds louder at night… or the night is quieter.

b.say: …the river is louder tonight.

a.say: Hoo… six points. You said a snowflake {var:snow_w}.

b.say: …this one too, I think.

a.say: Snowy morning… the meadow is very hushful.

b.say: …hushful morning. Snow on everything.

a.say: …our circle of light. You said the lantern {var:lantern_w}.

b.say: …let's sit in it a while.

a.say: The lantern glows extra warm tonight.

b.say: …lantern on. Night cozy.

a.say: …a closed pinecone. You said a pinecone {var:pinecone_w}.

b.say: …it'll open when it's ready.

a.say: Afternoon pinecones… warm and a little sticky.

b.say: …warm pinecones in the sun.

a.say: Oh… blink, blink. You said a firefly {var:firefly}.

b.say: …I blinked back. Twice.

a.say: Dusk fireflies… the meadow is lighting up.

b.say: …the meadow is lighting up.

a.say: …slow clouds tonight. You said a cloud {var:cloud_w}.

b.say: …two just met. Softly.

a.say: Big slow clouds today… lovely.

b.say: …slow clouds today. Lovely.

a.say: …red and orange. You said the leaves {var:leaves_w}.

b.say: …the tree looks very fancy.

a.say: Leaves drifting in the afternoon light… golden.

b.say: …golden leaves in the afternoon.

a.say: (Settles.) …You said bedtime {var:bedtime}.

b.say: …soft ones tonight, I hope.

a.say: Evening… almost story time.

b.say: …almost story time.

a.say: …purple again. You said the purple sky {var:sky_purple}.

b.say: …there's the first star. On time.

a.say: Dusk… my favorite in-between time.

b.say: …in-between time. My favorite.

a.say: …the band is tuning up. You said the cricket band {var:mouse_w}.

b.say: …a slow song tonight.

a.say: The night band is playing… the crickets are in tune tonight.

b.say: …the night band is tuning up.

a.say: (Fluffs the nest.) …You said a nest {var:nest}.

b.say: …cozier already.

a.say: Morning birds are singing near the nest… lovely.

b.say: …birds singing near it.

a.say: …snuffle, snuffle. You said the hedgehog {var:hedgehog}.

b.say: …we'll give it room.

a.say: Evening is hedgehog time… they come out with the crickets.

b.say: …hedgehog time. Snuffle.

a.say: Mm-mm… You said a hum {var:music_box}.

b.say: …I'm feeling it in my feathers.

a.say: Evening humming… it fits the quiet.

b.say: …an evening hum.

a.say: …the far hill is blue. You said it {var:far_hill}.

b.say: …wearing a bit of sky again.

a.say: The far hill is very clear today… I can see its trees.

b.say: …the far hill is clear today.

a.say: …a still puddle. You said a puddle {var:puddle_w}.

b.say: {pet_phrase} I won't step in. Just in case.

a.say: Morning puddles… full of morning sky.

b.say: …morning puddles, full of sky.

a.say: (Slow blink.) …You said a slow blink {var:owl_eyes}.

b.say: …that one was for you.

a.say: Evening blinks… extra slow ones.

b.say: …extra slow evening blinks.

a.say: …a shiny line. You said the snail {var:snail_w}.

b.say: …pretty, across the stone.

a.say: Morning snail… we're both slow in the morning.

b.say: …we're both slow this morning.

a.say: (Stretches.) …You said wings {var:wings}.

b.say: …folded now. Staying here.

a.say: Morning wing stretch… one, and then the other.

b.say: …a big morning stretch.

a.say: …my chipped cup. You said it {var:teacup_w}.

b.say: …still my favorite. Gently.

a.say: Afternoon tea cups… resting between teas.

b.say: …teacups resting.

a.say: …tick, tock. You said the clock {var:clock}.

b.say: …tick. Rest. Tock. Work.

a.say: The clock is louder at night… everything else is resting.

b.say: …the clock is loud tonight.

a.say: …swoop. You said a bat {var:bat}.

b.say: …busy evening for bats again.

a.say: Dusk bats are out… zipping around the trees.

b.say: …the dusk bats are out.

a.say: Hoo… lace on the window. You said the frost {var:frost}.

b.say: …it did a {word:soft} job.

a.say: Frosty morning… the window is sparkleful.

b.say: …sparkleful window this morning.

a.say: (Rests on the bark.) …You said the old tree {var:tree_old}.

b.say: …kind wrinkles. Still.

a.say: The old tree's shade is cool this afternoon.

b.say: …cool shade this afternoon.

a.say: …rustle, rustle. You said the rustling {var:night_sounds}.

b.say: …settling down now. Shh.

a.say: The night sounds are tuning up… lovely.

b.say: …the night sounds are tuning up.

a.say: …a round face in the spoon. You said it {var:honey}.

b.say: …my ears are huge again.

a.say: Breakfast spoons… shiny in the morning.

b.say: …shiny breakfast spoons.

a.say: …munch, munch. You said the caterpillar {var:caterpillar}.

b.say: …small, busy sound. Still.

a.say: Afternoon munching… the caterpillar is busy.

b.say: …busy munching today.

a.say: …orange everywhere. You said sunset orange {var:sunset}.

b.say: …just a little pink left now.

a.say: The sunset is slow tonight… taking its time.

b.say: …a slow sunset tonight.

a.say: Oh… a new mushroom. You said a mushroom {var:mushroom}.

b.say: …nice hat, little one.

a.say: Morning mushrooms… they come up with the dew.

b.say: …dew and mushrooms. Morning things.

a.say: …round and round. You said a seashell {var:seashell}.

b.say: …a {word:soft} shape. Still.

a.say: Afternoon sun on the seashell… it's all pink inside.

b.say: …the shell is pink in the sun.

a.say: (Tiny yawn.) …You said a yawn {var:yawn_w}.

b.say: …there's another. Very polite.

a.say: Morning yawns… there will be many.

b.say: …morning yawns. Many.

a.say: …our star map. You said it {var:map_stars}.

b.say: …I drew it big. In the corner.

a.say: Clear sky tonight… good for star maps.

b.say: …a clear sky. Good for maps.

a.say: (Looks up slowly.) …The moon is only half there tonight.

b.say: Where do you think… the other half went?

choices.label: It's sleeping
choices.reply: Hoo… half asleep. I know that feeling very well.
choices.memory: You told me… the moon sleeps half at a time

choices.label: It's hiding
choices.reply: Behind the dark… like peeking round a door.
choices.memory: You told me… the moon hides its other half

choices.label: Someone took a bite
choices.reply: A moon bite… hm. It must taste like cool milk.
choices.memory: You told me… the moon had a bite taken

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Mm… I think it's still there. Just resting in the dark.

c.say: …It grows back, you know. A little each night.

d.say: Half a moon… is still a whole friend.

a.say: …When the moon is on the water, it makes a silver path.

b.say: Where would the silver path take us?

choices.label: To the moon
choices.reply: To the moon… we'd walk very softly. It's a bright floor.

choices.label: To an island
choices.reply: A little moon island… with one tree. And quiet.

choices.label: Back home
choices.reply: Hoo… a path that leads home. The best kind.

c.say: (Slow blink.) …We'll walk it in our heads tonight.

a.say: Shall I hum… a little moon song?

choices.label: Yes, please
choices.reply: (Hums.) Mmm-mm… mm… That's all of it. Short… like a yawn.

choices.label: Just quiet
choices.reply: Quiet is a moon song too… the quietest kind.

b.say: {pet_phrase} Thank you for listening, little moon.

a.say: (Ears turn.) …Chirp… chirp. They never stop.

b.say: How do you think… crickets make their sound?

choices.label: With their legs
choices.reply: Leg music… hm. I have tried. I only have feathers.
choices.memory: You told me… the crickets play music with their legs

choices.label: They sing
choices.reply: Tiny voices… all together. A choir in the grass.
choices.memory: You told me… the crickets sing with tiny voices

choices.label: Little bells
choices.reply: Bells inside them… that would explain the twinkle.
choices.memory: You told me… the crickets have little bells inside

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Mm… perhaps by rubbing something. Like rubbing sleepy eyes.

c.say: …However they do it… it sounds like nighttime breathing.

a.say: …Do you hear that one? It's a little off-beat.

b.say: Do you think it's the youngest cricket?

choices.label: Yes, still learning
choices.reply: Still learning… we all are. It's doing very well.

choices.label: It's making its own song
choices.reply: Its own song… hoo. I like that one best now.

choices.label: @pool:giggle
choices.reply: Hoo-hoo… yes. It's a giggly cricket.

c.say: …Chirp… (chirp). There. I joined the off-beat one.

a.say: …Pit… pat. Pit-pat-pat. The rain is busy tonight.

b.say: What do you think rain is… before it falls?

choices.label: Cloud water
choices.reply: Cloud water… so clouds are wet pillows. Hm.
choices.memory: You told me… the rain starts as cloud water

choices.label: The sea
choices.reply: Sea that went for a visit… and is coming down to tell us.
choices.memory: You told me… the rain started as the sea

choices.label: Sky sprinkles
choices.reply: Sprinkles… the sky is watering its flowers.
choices.memory: You told me… the rain is the sky watering flowers

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Hm… I think rain is water on a long journey.

c.say: {pet_phrase} Welcome down, little drops. Mind the leaves.

a.say: (Sniffs.) …Do you smell that? After rain.

b.say: What does after-rain smell like… to you?

choices.label: Grass
choices.reply: Green grass… yes. Like the ground woke up.

choices.label: Wet stones
choices.reply: Wet stones… cool and old. I like that one.

choices.label: @pool:unsure
choices.reply: Hard to say… some smells don't have words. That's alright.

c.say: (Deep breath.) …Mmm. Smells like the world got a bath.

a.say: …There are so many stars tonight. More than feathers.

b.say: Do you think stars… talk to each other?

choices.label: By twinkling
choices.reply: Twinkle talk… a blink means hello, I think.
choices.memory: You told me… the stars talk by twinkling

choices.label: They're quiet
choices.reply: Quiet friends… just shining near each other.
choices.memory: You told me… the stars are quiet friends

choices.label: They whisper
choices.reply: Whispers… too far for us to hear. Even my ears.
choices.memory: You told me… the stars whisper to each other

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Mm… maybe they don't need words. Like us, sometimes.

c.say: (Slow blink at the sky.) …I said hello. In twinkle.

a.say: If a star heard a wish… what would yours be?

choices.label: Something for someone
choices.reply: For someone else… hoo. That's a generous wish.

choices.label: Something fun
choices.reply: Something fun… I hope it twinkles right down to you.

choices.label: Keep it inside
choices.reply: Keep it inside… yes. Some wishes like being cozy.

b.say: {pet_phrase} The stars are good listeners. Like you.

a.say: (Turns a page with one feather.) …Books smell old and kind.

b.say: Why do old books smell like this?

choices.label: Lots of stories
choices.reply: Stories piled up… they leave a smell. Like toast.
choices.memory: You told me… old books smell like piled stories

choices.label: They were trees
choices.reply: Trees once… that's a forest smell, then.
choices.memory: You told me… old books smell like the forest

choices.label: They're tired
choices.reply: Tired from being read… a good tired.
choices.memory: You told me… old books are pleasantly tired

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Hm… I think it's the smell of many hands being gentle.

c.say: (Sniffs the page.) …Toast and forest. My favorite chapter.

a.say: …If we wrote a book… it would need a name.

b.say: What should our book be called?

choices.label: The Night Book
choices.reply: The Night Book… simple and true. I'd read it.

choices.label: Whimber's Ears
choices.reply: Whimber's Ears… hoo-hoo. A very fluffy book.

choices.label: Two Friends
choices.reply: Two Friends… oh. I'd keep that one by my nest.

c.say: …Chapter one… “Once there was a {word:soft} evening.”

a.say: (Feathers ruffle.) …The wind is in a hurry tonight.

b.say: What is the wind hurrying for?

choices.label: A party
choices.reply: A sky party… it's late. Everyone's flying over.
choices.memory: You told me… the wind hurries to a sky party

choices.label: To get home
choices.reply: Going home… even wind has somewhere cozy.
choices.memory: You told me… the wind hurries home

choices.label: Chasing leaves
choices.reply: Leaf chasing… hm. It never catches them. Or always does.
choices.memory: You told me… the wind chases leaves

choices.label: @pool:listen
